- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 85.30 → 85.66), then fails to correct downward.
- Underestimates when true values show strong downward momentum (e.g., 85.66 → 75.36), especially after 10–15 days.
- Forecasts tend to be too smooth; fails to capture sudden drops or spikes in true values.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled — model holds onto high values longer than observed.
- Model often lags behind true values by 3–7 days, especially in downward trends.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values in the first 10 days, then drifts toward lower values.
- Model underestimates when true values are near or below 75.00, especially after a spike.
